correctness.rationale: For n≥4 the rank of right multiplication by {0,n} is 2^(n−1) and is uniquely maximal among nonidentity elements; for n=2,3 idempotency resolves the single other maximal-rank case. Other multi-positive sets have rank≤2^(n−2); other singletons exclude explicit target sets. The characteristic ideal generated by {0,n} is isomorphic to T_(n−1); induction and multiplication by {0,n} force every remaining set fixed. All cases n≥1 are proved symbolically. Independently implemented direct-set and bitmask tests through n=8 confirm base cases, ranks, quotient and associative multiplication, returning VERIFY_OK.

broader_coverage.reasoning: An automorphism of a monoid quotient does not generally lift to an automorphism of the source; the existence of a source automorphism does not imply a quotient automorphism. Reversion demonstrably fails to descend: {0,1} and {0,1,n+2} agree after truncation but have reversions that do not. The finite abelian group monoid uses modular addition, inapplicable to truncation. None of the inspected broader results subsumes all finite cutoff automorphism groups.

value.rationale: Complete all-n automorphism classification for a natural 2^n-element family of quotients of the reduced nonnegative power monoid. The result exposes a substantive quotient-symmetry failure: the globally nontrivial reversion disappears at every finite cutoff. The intrinsic terminal idempotent and its ideal supply a structural rigidity mechanism of possible use in finite convolution quotient analyses; not a selected arbitrary n or known-table recomputation.
